concepts.why: The patient has a history of prosthetic mitral valve thrombosis and presents with symptoms of dyspnea on exertion, orthopnea, and paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, which are consistent with valve thrombosis.
The patient has a hemoglobin level of 9.65 g/dL, which is below the normal range, indicating anemia.
The patient presents with fever, elevated inflammatory markers, and a history of valve repair, which are consistent with infective endocarditis.

The patient has a history of rheumatic mitral stenosis and presents with symptoms of dyspnea on exertion, orthopnea, and paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, which are consistent with rheumatic heart disease.
The patient has an elevated prothrombin time and INR, which are consistent with disseminated intravascular coagulation.

rationales.F01: Dyspnea on exertion is a common symptom of prosthetic valve thrombosis.
rationales.F02: Orthopnea and paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea are indicative of heart failure, which can be caused by prosthetic valve thrombosis.
rationales.F08: Low hemoglobin is a key indicator of anemia.
rationales.F10: Prolonged prothrombin time and elevated INR are indicative of coagulopathy, which can be seen in prosthetic valve thrombosis and disseminated intravascular coagulation.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient presents with fever, bilateral knee pain, elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate, and positive C-reactive protein, which are indicative of an infectious process, and the absence of other systemic symptoms or findings suggestive of alternative diagnoses makes Infective endocarditis the most likely explanation.
